condition.narrative: Finance Agreement : Safeguards | Description: The Recipient shall ensure that the Project is carried out in accordance withtheSafeguard Instruments.

Finance Agreement :Safety and Security Levy | Description: The Recipient shall take all measures required on its part to ensurethat AVL shall, from not later than July 1, 2016, and thereafter throughout the Project implementation period, collect fromdeparting international passengers a levy in a minimum amount equivalent to five Australian Dollars (AU$5) to recover aviationsafety and security expenditures incurred by the Recipient.

Financing Agreement :Program Steering Committee | Description :The Recipient shall nominate the chairman of the VPMU SteeringCommittee (or their designated representative) as its member to the Program Steering Committee. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Financing Agreement :Regional Procurement Evaluation Committee | Description :The Recipient shall, in collaboration with the otherProgram Countries, ensure that the Regional Procurement Evaluation Committee is maintained throughout the Project implementationperiod and comprised of representatives of the Program Countries, TAL (through TFSU) and PASO. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

Financing Agreement :VPMU | Description :The VPMU shall be maintained throughout the Project implementation period with adequateresources and competent and qualified staff in adequate numbers required for the Project. | Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Navigation and safety aids in line with implementation schedule

comment.narrative: <p>Activity was not implemented under project due to project funds shortfall. The Government of Vanuatu has confirmed an allocationof VUV 700 million (equivalent to US$ 6.3 million) in July 2019 to finance this activity as a part of the project.  </p>

title.narrative: Navigation and safety aids in line with implementation schedule
Grievances responded and/or resolved within the stipulated services standards for response times

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Two complaints were received during the project time and were addressed in a timely manner. </p>

title.narrative: Repairs to Bauerfieled, Whitegrass and Pekoa Airport pavements in line with implementation schedule

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Repair works were completed at all three airports but with 9-month delay at Bauerfield, 3-month delay at Whitegrass and 1-month delay at Pekoa.</p>

title.narrative: Airport Master Plan in line with implementation schedule

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The Airport Master Plan was delivered in December 2018 after 6-month delay. </p>

title.narrative: Aviation Sector Strategy in line with implementation schedule

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The Aviation Sector Strategy was delivered in November 2017.</p>

title.narrative: Grievance registered related to delivery of project benefits by gender that are actually addressed

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Two Grievances were submitted under the project and addressed.</p>

State requirements for safety measured by Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP) reaches global ICAO average
State requirements for safety measured by Universal Safety Oversight Audit Programme (USOAP) reaches global ICAO average

comment.narrative: <p>Not achieved. The updated USOAP audit did not take place for Vanuatu as of project completion, therefore it is not possible to assess if the project intervention has contributed to a better audit result. This PDO indicator is deemed at ICR as ineffective to measure the project outcome. </p>

<p>Achieved. Two refurbished fire tender vehicles (FTVs) were delivered in September 2018 after 3-month delay. Counting in oneexisting FTV financed by JICA, the number of FTVs at Bauerfield is now qualified for Category 8 Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting operations.</p>

title.narrative: Project-supported organization(s) publishing periodic reports on GRM and how issues were resolved

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved. Project's website (www.vaip.vu) displays the resolution rate for grievances. However, time to resolve the grievances and how the issues were resolved were not published.</p>

title.narrative: Successful implementation of agreed training plan

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved. Training Needs Assessments for CAAV and AVL were delivered in February 2018, which include a proposed training program. Due to project fund shortfall, training programs proposed were not implemented. </p>

actual.value: Training Plan developed but not implemented

title.narrative: Successful implementation of agreed training plan
Modernization of air traffic management achieved

actual.value: ADS-B and VSAT installed and fully operational

title.narrative: Modernization of air traffic management achieved

comment.narrative: <p>Partially achieved. Supply and installation of ADS-B Ground Stations were completed at Bauerfield and Pekoa in November 2018 and are fully operational on screen. About 70% aircrafts on the domestic registry have been installed with ADS-B Out Avionics. AVLis coordinating with airlines to schedule installation for the remaining fleets. Civil works for VSAT have been completed at all three airports. Devices have been procured and transported to Vanuatu and are currently under installation.</p>

title.narrative: Regional safety and security levy for departing international passengers implemented

comment.narrative: <p>The target was achieved. Starting from 1 September 2017, an SSL of AU$5 for each departing international passenger was activated. The implementation of the SSL is a dated legal covenant that was expected to be completed not later than 1 July 2016. The introduction of the levy was delayed due to the process associated with legislative amendment to Vanuatu's Civil Aviation Act to authorize the collection. </p>

actual.value: AU$5 safety and security levy is being collected from each departing international passenger.

title.narrative: Emergency Repairs to Bauerfieled and Whitegrass completed

baseline.value: No spot rehabilitations at Bauerfield/ Damages from Cyclone Pam at Whitegrass not repaired

target.value: Bauerfield runway remains operational/Whitegrass meets safety requirements

actual.value: Three sets of emergency repairs at Bauerfield are completed; Whitegrass repairs (fencing, building) damaged by Cyclone repairedwith 60% completed.

title.narrative: Emergency Repairs to Bauerfieled and Whitegrass completed

baseline.value: No spot rehabilitations at Bauerfield/ Damages from Cyclone Pam at Whitegrass not repaired

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. Emergency reconstruction works for both Bauerfield and Whitegrass airport are completed. The originally planned repairing works for the Whitegrass Terminal was dropped at Mid-Term Review as the AVL had completed the repairing works with its own resource.</p>

actual.value: Three sets of emergency repairs at Bauerfield are completed; Whitegrass repairs (fencing, staff house) damaged by Cyclone repaired.

title.narrative: Project-supported organization(s) publishing periodic reports on GRM and how issues were resolved
Regulatory certification of safety and security at Bauerfield (VLI) maintained

comment.narrative: <p>Achieved. The Baurfield Airport (VLI) has renewed its status as a CAAV certified airport in May 2019. This indicates that the aerodrome design and operations at VLI, based on the inspection carried out by CAAV with support from PASO, are now compliant with the safety and security standards required by Vanuatu Civil Aviation Rules (Part 139) and applicable portions of ICAO Annex 14.</p>

actual.value: CAAV renewed the Aerodromes Operators Certificate for VLI
